### Karl-Dai/IEC60870-5-104-Simulator
- URL: https://github.com/Karl-Dai/IEC60870-5-104-Simulator
- Exact commit / revision: `04c8ee363b95ef0af75eab44efff507fdb026053`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- What it contains: MIT Rust/Tauri IEC 60870-5-104 desktop lab implementing both Master and Slave, TCP/mutual-TLS, monitored/control ASDUs, multi-CA links, direct execute and Select-Before-Operate, GI/counter interrogation/clock sync, negative confirmations, auto-reconnect, live connection state, event replay, traffic decode and CSV export.
- Rare or undernoticed value: It is not merely a protocol library; it is a ready two-ended operator test bench with stateful point models, event playback and protocol-correct failure behavior. Recent work reports 108 Master and 305 Slave tests and fixes TLS race behavior.
- Likely buyer / user: Utility/substation integrators, RTU/IED vendors, SCADA vendors, industrial gateway teams and commissioning labs.
- Painful problem: IEC-104 changes are commonly tested against scarce hardware or a single vendor stack, leaving handshake, command, CA, TLS and reconnect edge cases until commissioning.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Fixed-price IEC-104 gateway/RTU acceptance pack: import a customer's point model, replay events, execute control/GI/TLS/reconnect cases, and deliver a compatibility evidence report before plant cutover.
- Build-time / data advantage: Roughly 3-6+ months of dual-ended protocol/UI/test-bench work plus substantial IEC-104 edge-case discovery.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact current revision and recent test/release commits; MIT LICENSE; README protocol matrix and operational workflows; `crates/iec104sim-core/src/slave.rs` search evidence showing STARTDT/STOPDT-aware session state and Rust unit tests.
- License / rights: MIT. IEC standards documents and customer device models remain separate rights sources.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable under MIT.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: A young 2026 project framed as a desktop simulator rather than a commercial conformance lab, yet it already has unusually broad master/slave behavior and operator tooling.
- Value score: **29/30** — A5, B4, C5, D5, E5, F5. Revenue can start as services quickly; ceiling is somewhat narrower than a general industrial platform.
- Combination opportunities: Make this the permissive operator-facing IEC-104 bench, then cross-check against `digitalpetri/iec60870` and GPL `mz-automation/lib60870`; add ProtoForge for broader fault/scenario orchestration.
- Next action: Run one shared fixture across Karl-Dai, DigitalPetri and lib60870 covering STARTDT/STOPDT/TESTFR, I/S/U sequencing, GI, SBO/direct commands, unknown IOA/type, reconnect, TLS and malformed/timeout cases.

### digitalpetri/iec60870
- URL: https://github.com/digitalpetri/iec60870
- Exact commit / revision: `d287840655b7942ee4e01222984cc64a734e4d67`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong
- What it contains: Java 17/Netty IEC 60870-5 implementation covering CS104 plus CS101 serial/101-over-TCP, raw ASDU access and high-level controlling/controlled-station APIs. Its APCI engine explicitly owns V(S)/V(R), k/w windows, t1/t2/t3 timers, I/S/U frames, STARTDT/STOPDT roles, sequence validation and queue policy.
- Rare or undernoticed value: The repository includes cross-module integration tests including TLS and a dedicated interoperability suite against lib60870-C peer images through Testcontainers, giving an independent protocol oracle rather than another self-test.
- Likely buyer / user: Utility protocol vendors, SCADA/RTU gateway teams, OEMs and testing labs.
- Painful problem: IEC-101/104 interoperability defects emerge from state-machine/timer/sequence differences between implementations, not only from basic ASDU encoding.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Independent Java comparator inside an IEC-104/101 migration and regression lab, sold as pre-cutover validation or continuous firmware/gateway regression.
- Build-time / data advantage: Saves several months of link/session state-machine, serial/TCP/TLS and interop-harness engineering.
- Concrete evidence inspected: README module/interop/test descriptions; `iec60870-cs104/.../ApciSession.java` state machine; exact revision; EPL-2.0 LICENSE.
- License / rights: EPL-2.0.
- Reuse classification: Reusable with EPL-2.0 obligations; especially attractive as an isolated comparator/test service if a permissive product core is preferred.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Pre-1.0 Java library; its highest value is hidden in the state-machine detail and lib60870 cross-stack interop tests.
- Value score: **26/30** — A4, B4, C5, D5, E5, F3. Rights are clear but weak-copyleft and API is pre-release.
- Combination opportunities: Karl-Dai + DigitalPetri + lib60870 forms a three-implementation IEC acceptance matrix; ProtoForge can contribute generic fault injection and evidence orchestration.
- Next action: Pin the lib60870 Testcontainers peer and compare identical failure/timer cases against Karl-Dai before selecting the canonical test-oracle strategy.

### open62541/open62541
- URL: https://github.com/open62541/open62541
- Exact commit / revision: `f223658c6ff9b9aca1591b8fbb2d4b87e68706f5`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender component
- What it contains: Mature C OPC UA client/server stack with discovery, security, information-model/code-generation, PubSub and embedded portability. The project reports an officially certified v1.4 Standard Server profile and an extensive quality regime including OPC Foundation CTT, unit coverage, fuzzing and memory/static analysis.
- Rare or undernoticed value: For the current hunt it is most valuable as an independent, certification-oriented OPC UA oracle rather than as another gateway library. The test tree includes read/write, encoding/chunking/event-loop and broad protocol tests, while current commits continue fixing PubSub semantics.
- Likely buyer / user: Industrial gateway vendors, machine builders, OPC UA server/client vendors and OT integration labs.
- Painful problem: OPC UA gateways can appear functional while failing session, security, type, subscription, information-model or PubSub edge cases against a different stack.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Cross-stack OPC UA compatibility diagnostic using customer endpoints plus three independent open implementations, with regression evidence delivered before firmware/gateway releases.
- Build-time / data advantage: Years of protocol, security and conformance engineering; avoids creating an independent oracle from scratch.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Current revision; MPL-2.0 LICENSE; README commercial-use boundary, certification claim and quality gates; root/tests tree including high-level read/write and encoding/chunking tests.
- License / rights: MPL-2.0; separate files can remain proprietary, while modifications to MPL-covered files follow MPL terms. Third-party NodeSet/spec artifacts require their own terms.
- Reuse classification: Reusable with MPL-2.0 conditions.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Well-known as a library, but the monetizable value here is as a certification-grade independent comparator inside a managed acceptance lab.
- Value score: **27/30** — A4, B5, C5, D4, E5, F4.
- Combination opportunities: ProtoForge process/fault orchestration + open62541 + node-opcua + OT Fabric Go OPC UA creates a cross-language OPC UA acceptance matrix.
- Next action: Define a protocol-neutral fixture for secure session lifecycle, browse/read/write, bad NodeId/type, reconnect, subscription recovery and malformed/timeout behavior across the three stacks.

### openconfig/featureprofiles
- URL: https://github.com/openconfig/featureprofiles
- Exact commit / revision: `320a002461732a27c491b63cec68efd198aa2c0e`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- What it contains: Active Apache-2.0 OpenConfig behavior/conformance corpus: feature-path definitions plus Ondatra tests spanning gNMI/gNOI/gRIBI and routing/network features, runnable against virtual devices through KNE or real hardware through bindings. It includes platform exception metadata keyed by vendor, hardware-model regex and software-version regex.
- Rare or undernoticed value: This closes the exact missing layer in the current Clixon/notconf/Netopeer2/gnmic lab: real-device behavioral expectations and vendor/model/version deviations rather than another protocol client. Deviation metadata covers operational quirks such as OS install/activation reboot behavior, gNOI component reboot/status paths, OpenConfig path gaps and numerous BGP/ISIS/QoS/platform differences.
- Likely buyer / user: Network operators, NOS vendors, NMS/controller vendors, telecom integrators and MSPs performing multi-vendor automation migrations.
- Painful problem: An OpenConfig/gNMI controller can pass against synthetic endpoints yet fail on specific NOS versions because supposedly standard behaviors, paths and lifecycle operations differ.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Fixed-price network automation readiness report for a customer's model/version matrix: run selected Feature Profiles against permitted virtual/physical devices, map deviations and produce pass/fail/remediation evidence before controller cutover.
- Build-time / data advantage: Potentially 6-12+ months of standards test design and vendor-specific exception discovery; ongoing upstream work continually adds behavior tests.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Current 2026-09-19 revision; Apache-2.0 LICENSE; README test framework and virtual/real hardware flows; `internal/deviations/deviations.go` compliance-tier logic; `proto/metadata.proto` vendor/model/software exception fields and concrete gNOI/OpenConfig deviations; current transceiver streaming-telemetry test commit.
- License / rights: Apache-2.0 for repository code. Vendor NOS/container images, hardware and some external model/spec artifacts retain separate licenses.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable code/tests under Apache-2.0, subject to external image/model rights.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Known in OpenConfig engineering circles, but its commercial moat is the accumulated behavior/deviation corpus and its fit as the evidence layer atop an independent controller/simulator lab.
- Value score: **29/30** — A4, B5, C5, D5, E5, F5.
- Combination opportunities: `clixon-controller + notconf + Netopeer2 + gnmic + FeatureProfiles/Ondatra` becomes a full migration-acceptance system: synthetic scale, independent NETCONF server, gNMI tooling and real NOS behavior/deviation tests.
- Next action: Select 15-25 high-value profiles covering configuration transactions, telemetry, gNOI lifecycle and routing; execute against at least one permitted virtual NOS and emit a normalized compatibility matrix.

- Likely buyer / user: Operators and MSPs modernizing device automation while still carrying CLI-only or mixed-capability fleets.

- Build-time / data advantage: Saves weeks to months of pager/prompt/error/vendor session handling and serverization.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact current commit; MIT LICENSE; README vendor/NETCONF/gRPC/HTTP capabilities; code-search hit in `pkg/device/netconf/device_mock_test.go` containing realistic vendor capability responses.

- Reuse classification: Directly reusable under MIT.
